title: free-disk-space capabilities
description: What the binary can do to reclaim space on the user's Mac, grouped by responsibility. None of them checks who calls; each acts with the invoking user's file permissions.

entities.name: In-place compression of inactive files
entities.description: Finds large, old, compressible files and compresses them transparently with APFS compression.
entities.responsibility: Keeps a resumable scan of a directory tree in a state file, estimates each file's saving from samples, and compresses chosen candidates in place only after verifying the compressed copy.
access: Any local user who can run the binary; the scan sees what that user can read.
A file is compressed only if its directory is writable by the user, no process has it open, and it is unchanged since the scan.
Compressing needs macOS (ditto and APFS); elsewhere it refuses unless FDS_FORCE is set.
It does not start when ditto's probe copy does not come out compressed.
On a terminal the user confirms the plan unless --yes is given.

entities.name: Clone dedupe
entities.description: Turns identical copies of a file into copy-on-write clones of one copy.
entities.responsibility: From the file names the scan recorded, hashes same-named, same-sized files and replaces identical ones on the same volume with verified APFS clones of a kept copy, keeping each file's own metadata.
access: Any local user; nothing changes without --apply.
Without --include-system only files the user owns, not owned by root, and outside system paths are considered.
A file is replaced only if it is single-linked, writable, in a writable directory, not open, not flagged and not already replaced by an earlier dedupe of the same scan.
--apply needs macOS (clonefile); elsewhere it refuses unless FDS_FORCE is set.

entities.name: Cleanup of regenerable files
entities.description: Deletes files that can be downloaded or built again, and empties the Downloads folder and the Trash when asked.
entities.responsibility: Empties fixed cache folders and the chosen targets, deletes dev build artifacts it can prove are regenerable, old and unused, and prunes Homebrew and an already-running Docker Desktop. An applying run that was interrupted resumes, the next time, after the steps it finished.
access: Any local user; nothing is deleted without --apply.
What the user may not delete is listed as protected and left.
Docker is touched only when it is already running; it is never started.

entities.name: Background cleaning
entities.description: Keeps free space above a threshold without the user asking each time.
entities.responsibility: Checks free space on the data volume every cadence of awake time and runs clean --apply on the chosen targets when it is below the threshold; installs, removes and reports itself as the user's launchd login item.
access: Installed per user, in the user's own launchd gui domain; it deletes with that user's permissions.
Once installed it deletes without asking, on the targets fixed at install time.
